title: ATAC-seq protocol for the profiling of chromatin accessibility of in situ fixed quiescent and activated muscle stem cells
protocol: Prepare 30 mL of ice-cold PBS in a 50 mL falcon tube and label it with "PBS".
Prepare 30 mL of ice-cold 0.5% PFA solution in a 50 mL falcon tube and label it with "PFA".
Prepare 30 mL of ice-cold 2 M Glycine solution in a 50 mL falcon tube and label it with "Glycine".
Store the prepared solutions on ice.
Set up the perfusion pump with a speed of 70–80 rpm.
Anesthetize the mouse with 2,2,2-Tribromoethanol (Avertin) through intraperitoneal injection.
Only proceed to the next step when the mouse stops moving.
Pinch the mouse on the sole to check whether it is fully anesthetized.
Administer an additional dose of anesthetization reagent if needed.
Immobilize the mouse with pins/needles on plastic foam.
Open the chest and expose the heart for perfusion.
Make an incision on the right atrium for fluid removal.
Hold the heart with blunt-end forceps and pierce the heart near the bottom of the left ventricle with the butterfly needle.
Perfuse the mouse with PBS for 3 min or until the pumped-out solution becomes clear.
Perfuse the mouse with 0.5% PFA for 5 min.
Perfuse the mouse with 2 M Glycine for 3 min to quench the PFA fixation.
Prepare a 10 cm glass petri-dish with 10 mL of wash medium for each mouse.
Dissect the hindlimb muscles and put them into the petri-dish.
Transfer all muscles of a mouse to a fresh Petri dish.
Mince the muscles in the dissociation buffer until no large pieces can be seen.
Transfer minced muscle pieces to a 50 mL falcon tube with 10 mL of muscle dissociation buffer.
Seal the tube with Parafilm.
Incubate in a 37°C shaking water bath at 65–70 rpm for 90 minutes.
Top up the tube to 50 mL with cold wash medium after digestion.
Centrifuge cells at 500 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Aspirate supernatant down to 10 mL.
Add 1 mL of stock Collagenase II solution and 1 mL of stock Dispase solution.
Resuspend the pellet with a 10 mL serological pipette.
Triturate until the pellet is fully suspended.
Fill the tube to 30 mL with cold wash medium.
Seal the tube with Parafilm.
Incubate in a 37°C water bath at 65–70 rpm for 30 minutes.
Aspirate and eject the muscle suspension 10 times using a 30 mL syringe and a 20-gauge needle after digestion.
Place a 40 μm nylon cell strainer on a new 50 mL falcon tube.
Transfer the cell suspension to the new tube through the cell strainer.
Add 10 mL of wash medium to the original tube, swirl to rinse, then transfer it through the same cell strainer.
Collect any remaining liquid on the underside of the strainer using a 200 μL pipette.
Top up the tube to 50 mL with cold wash medium after rinsing.
Centrifuge tubes at 500 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C after collecting cells.
Remove all supernatant by aspiration immediately after centrifugation.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of wash medium.
Transfer the resuspended cells to the strainer cap attached to a 5 mL FACS tube.
Gently tap the tube to facilitate flow-through.
Set up the cell sorter following the manufacturer’s specifications with the 70-μm nozzle.
Create gates to collect the singlet GFP+ population into 500 μL of PBS in a 5 mL round-bottom FACS tube.
Pre-cool PBS and Lysis Buffer on ice before starting the ATAC-seq procedure.
Centrifuge the sorted cells at 2000 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Gently remove the supernatant using a 200 μL pipette.
Resuspend the cells with 50 μL cold PBS and centrifuge at 2000 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Gently remove the supernatant using a 200 μL pipette.
Resuspend the cells with 50 μL Lysis buffer and centrifuge at 2000 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Gently remove the supernatant using a 200 μL pipette.
Resuspend the cells with a 50 μL Tagmentation reaction mix.
Incubate the reaction mix at 37°C for 30 min in a thermomixer.
Add reverse crosslinking solution to the tagmented mixture.
Incubate at 65°C with agitation at 1000 rpm in a thermomixer for 12–16 h.
Purify the tagmented DNA with a PCR Cleanup kit.
Elute the purified DNA in 10 μL elution buffer.
Store purified DNA at −20°C if not used immediately.
Amplify the purified DNA for 5 cycles.
Determine the cycle number with qPCR for library amplification.
Amplify the rest of the previously PCR-amplified DNA with the additional number of cycles chosen based on fluorescence intensity.
Purify the DNA using AMPure XP beads with a size selection of 200 bp to 1 kb.
Top up the PCR product to 50 μL with Nuclease-free water.
Add 27.5 μL of beads (0.55×) and mix well.
Incubate at 20°C–22°C for 10 min.
Centrifuge briefly, then place the tube onto a magnetic rack for 2 min until the liquid becomes clear.
Carefully transfer the supernatant to a new tube and discard the beads.
Add 32.5 μL of beads (1.2×) to the supernatant from the previous step.
Mix well and incubate at 20°C–22°C for 10 min.
Centrifuge briefly, then place the tube onto a magnetic rack for 2 min until the liquid becomes clear.
Carefully remove and discard the supernatant.
Add 200 μL of freshly prepared 80% ethanol to the tube while on the magnetic rack without disturbing it.
Incubate at 20°C–22°C for 30 s and discard the supernatant.
Repeat this step once.
Completely remove the residual ethanol, and air-dry beads for 2 min while the tube is on the magnetic rack with the lid open.
Remove the tube from the magnetic rack and add 21 μL of nuclease-free water or elution buffer to elute DNA.
Mix thoroughly and incubate at 20°C–22°C for 5 min.
Centrifuge briefly and then place the tube back onto the magnetic rack until the liquid becomes clear.
Transfer 20 μL of supernatant to a new tube with no beads carry-over.
